results.title: BHCC Adults Community Support and Supported Living Light Touch Dynamic Purchasing System (DPS) Admission Round 4
results.description:
Brighton and Hove City Council (BHCC) established a Light Touch Dynamic Purchasing System (DPS) for the supply of services in respect of Community Support and Supported Living for adults on 4th March 2024 for an initial period of up to 5 years + with optional further extension provisions for an additional 3 years + 2 years. The end of the initial contract term of the DPS is 3rd March 2029. This Contract Notice is for the fourth admission round onto the DPS.
The services required fall under Schedule 3 of the Public Contracts Regulations 2015 (PCR 2015). As a result, this procurement is undertaken under the 'Light Touch Regime' as detailed in Section 7 of PCR 2015.
Any interested organisation or consortium with relevant experience may apply to be admitted onto the DPS.
The DPS will have two (2) lots and be further divided into sub-lots as follows:
Lot 1: Community Support
Lot 1.1: Adults with Learning Disabilities and who may also be autistic
Lot 1.2: Adults with Mental Health needs
Lot 1.3: Adults who are Neurodivergent and who may also be autistic
Lot 1.4: Adults with Acquired Brain Injuries (ABI)
Lot 1.5: Adults with Physical Disabilities and/or sensory needs
Lot 1.6: Adults with Substance Misuse and eligible Care Act needs
Lot 2: Supported Living, for people with:
Lot 2.1: Adults with Learning Disabilities and who may also be autistic
Lot 2.2: Adults with Mental Health needs
Lot 2.3: Adults who are Neurodivergent and who may also be autistic
Lot 2.4: Adults with Acquired Brain Injuries (ABI)
Lot 2.5: Adults with Physical Disabilities and/or sensory needs
Lot 2.6: Adults with Substance Misuse and eligible Care Act needs
Potential Providers are invited to apply for one lot or sub-lot; or multiple lots and sub-lots.
The Brighton & Hove commissioning strategy is to reduce the number of people in residential care, placed out of the city and in long term services that do not meet their needs. Supported Living and Community Support are effective in meeting this goal.
The aim of the DPS is to:
- Ensure that all providers on the DPS have met quality requirements and signed up to a new service specification that reflects the needs that people who receive support and their carers have identified.
- Attract new providers to the market and create a more diverse market that provides more choice for people who receive support.
- Ensure a more strengths-based approach that focus on outcomes for people who receive support.
- Enable the Council to meet the care and support needs of residents who have been assessed as having eligible social care needs in line with the Care Act 2014
For each Lot, there will be an 'Admission' stage, followed by a 'Commissioning' stage.
BHCC intends to open the 'Admission' stage annually for new applications. The Council reserves the right to revise the number of rounds ('opening ceremonies') for Admission stage per year at its discretion.
By applying to be admitted to the DPS, Providers are not obligated to bid for services at 'Commissioning' stage.
These services are being procured under a multiple-Provider DPS. There will be no limit to the number of Providers admitted onto the DPS, providing they meet the minimum requirements as set out in the Invitation to Tender documents.
There will be no guarantee of work or volume of work given under this DPS.
Admission stage evaluation will be based on 100% Quality.
For Lot 1: Community Support, Pricing will be requested and will be binding until 31st March 2028 but will not be scored. This pricing will be used at Stage 2: Commissioning Stage for Direct Awards.

results.title: Pitch & athletics facilities repairs & maintenance in non-domestic properties (measured term contract 2027)
results.description:
East Renfrewshire Council is seeking to appoint an experienced and suitably qualified supplier to provide maintenance and repairs services for school pitches and athletic tracks within the Council. The services will be planned and, as and when required.
This procurement will be conducted via the Public Contracts Scotland - Tender portal (PCS-T). We will apply a one stage Open procedure.
Bidders must self-certify their adherence to the conditions of participation via the SPD (Scotland) in PSC-T, and may be required to submit Means of Proof before contract award. Bidders must refer to the specific requirements listed in Section III in this OJEU Contract Notice when completing the SPD in PCS-T.
The Value shown in this notice is excluding VAT

results.title: Flexible Framework Agreement for the Provision of Alcohol and Drug Recovery Services and Supports in South and East Ayrshire
results.description:
This procurement exercise is a collaboration between South Ayrshire Council and East Ayrshire Council on behalf of the South Ayrshire Alcohol and Drug Partnership (SAADP) and the East Ayrshire Alcohol and Drug Partnership (EAADP), with South Ayrshire Council (the Council) acting as the lead contracting authority.
The Council has a requirement to establish a multi-lot Flexible Framework Agreement (FFA) comprising of a range of suitably qualified Service Providers capable of delivering high-quality alcohol and drug recovery services and supports.  The FFA is intended to create a flexible and sustainable framework through which the SAADP and EAADP can award call-off contracts and/or partnership agreements, either through direct award or by conducting a further competition.
The scope of the FFA falls within the ‘Social and Other Specific Services’ category and is subject to the procurement regimes set out under the Public Contracts (Scotland) Regulations 2015.
As such, this “Light Touch Regime” allows a flexible approach which will permit new entrants to submit tender offers for inclusion of services and supports on the FFA or will allow existing Service Providers to apply for inclusion of new services or supports to the FFA.

results.title: EDC/2026/4497 Framework Agreement for Drainage Civil Engineering Works
results.description: East Dunbartonshire Council wishes to establish a public contract (within the meaning of the Procurement Regulations) and appoint a number of suppliers under an overarching ranked framework arrangement to carry out work and provide Work Orders in relation to Drainage Civil Engineering Works throughout the local government area of East Dunbartonshire over a minimum period of three (3) years with an option to extend up to a further 12 months.

results.title: CP-401 - Aster Group External Decorations
results.description:
Aster Group is a housing association which provides quality, affordable homes to thousands of people across the south of England and London. Its vision is that everyone has a home. See our website for more details www.aster.co.uk/corporate/about-us
The not-for-dividend business was established in 1990 and has £2.5 billion worth of social housing assets. The Group reinvests profits from open market sale and shared ownership to support the development of affordable homes. It owns and maintains over 37,000 homes and employs over 2,000 people.
Central and Cecil Housing Trust (C&C), East Boro Housing Trust (EBHT) and Enham Trust form part of the Aster Group. For further information visit: www.ccht.org.uk, www.ebht.org.uk and www.enhamtrust.org.uk.
Aster Group Limited ("Aster") has a requirement for three contractors to provide External Decoration services, including but not limited to:
•	Redecoration of all previously painted external surfaces and internal common parts.
•	Minor external fabric repairs including:
o	Renewal of fascias and soffits where required (to match existing).
o	Renewal of timber canopies where required.
o	Repointing of brick work.
•	Minor prior to paint repairs.
•	Timber window repairs.
•	Renewal of communal floor finishes where required.
Aster's requirement is across its full geographical coverage and will be split into the following lots with the corresponding approx. number of properties:
•	Lot 1 (East)
o	Berkshire - 205
o	Hampshire - 8416
o	Oxfordshire - 612
o	Wiltshire (incl. Gloucestershire) - 8606
•	Lot 2 (London and Outer Areas)
o	London - 1969
o	Surrey - 441
o	Sussex - 736
•	Lot 3 (West)
o	Dorset - 803
o	Somerset (incl. Bristol) - 5339
o	Devon and Cornwall - 3208
NB: The property numbers are approximate and may make up multi dwelling properties.
Suppliers may submit bids for multiple lots; however, only one supplier will be awarded each lot. Where a supplier achieves the highest ranking in more than one lot, Aster Group reserves the right to determine which lot will be awarded to that supplier. In such circumstances, the lot not awarded to the highest-ranked supplier will instead be awarded to the supplier ranked second for that lot.
Aster's procurement for external decorations is anticipated to be a single stage tender process and will be undertaken via CHIC's All Under One Roof' DPS (Lot 20 - Decoration Services).
The evaluation criteria is anticipated to be 60/40 (price/quality).
Aster has a target start date of May 2027, by which point mobilisation should be completed (TUPE is applicable) and contractors are fully onboarded to Aster's Approved Supplier List and familiar with its Contractor Portal. By the contract start date, the contractor should ensure a fully resourced programme is made available to Aster.
The form of contract Aster anticipated to contract with is the JCT Measured Term Contract (2024 edition) containing Aster amendments.

results.title: SWAG Cancer Alliance Lung Cancer Screening Programme
results.description:
Bristol NHS Foundation Trust (BFT), as host organisation for the Somerset, Wiltshire, Avon and Gloucestershire (SWAG) Cancer Alliance, is seeking to appoint a provider to deliver a fully managed Lung Cancer Screening Programme across the Somerset, Wiltshire, Avon and Gloucestershire (SWAG) Cancer Alliance area. The procurement is being managed by Bristol and Weston NHS Purchasing Consortium (BWPC) on behalf of the Trust.
The service will identify and engage eligible populations, deliver lung cancer screening services, provide low-dose CT (LDCT) scanning services, and ensure effective management of participant pathways in support of the early detection and diagnosis of lung cancer.
The provider will be required to deliver a high-quality, accessible and equitable service that maximises uptake, reduces health inequalities, and complies with all relevant national standards and programme requirements.
The contract term is 36 months, with the option to extend for up to two further periods of 12 months each, giving a maximum total contract duration of 60 months. Additional information is contained within the Invitation to Tender documentation available through SAP Ariba.

results.title: Universal Stop Smoking Service
results.description:
The London Borough of Ealing is undertaking preliminary market engagement to inform the future procurement of a Universal Stop Smoking Service.

This notice is issued for the purposes of preliminary market engagement only and does not constitute a call for competition or commencement of a procurement process.

This premarket engagement and future procurement is being undertaken under the Health Care Services (Provider Selection Regime) Regulations 2023.

results.title: Sight Testing and Dispensing of Spectacles to Children and Young People in Special Educational Settings (SES) - South West
results.description:
This notice is inform the market of an opportunity to deliver Sight Testing and Dispensing of Spectacles to Children and Young People in Special Educational Settings within the South West region, covering Devon, Cornwall and Isles of Scilly (CIOS), Bristol, North Somerset and South Gloucestershire (BNSSG) and Gloucestershire Integrated Care Boards (ICBs). 
BNSSG, Gloucestershire, Devon and CIOS ICBs ('the Commissioner') are the contracting authorities for this procurement. The Commissioner may be subject to a restructure of its functions during or following this procurement process. In such circumstances, the functions to which this contract relates may be transferred to a successor or replacement public body. Bidders will be informed of any such change, and any changes because of it.
The procurement is divided into the following Lots: 
•	Lot 1: BNSSG and Gloucestershire
•	Lot 2: Devon and CIOS 
The contract(s) term will be for 3 years and 5 months (inclusive of the mobilisation period) plus a possible extension of up to a period of a further 2 years. Both contract(s) are due to commence on 01 April 2027 with service delivery anticipated to commence from 01 September 2027. 
The annual contract value for Lot 1 is £306,000 with a total maximum contract value of £1,530,000 (including extension option).
The annual contract value for Lot 2 is £350,000 with a total maximum contract value of £1,750,000 (including extension option). 
Interested parties who wish to take part in the procurement are invited to take part in an Invitation to Tender (ITT) process, based on the competitive 'open' procedure. All ITT responses must be returned by 12 noon on 10th December 2026.
Interested providers will be able to view the opportunity and access the tender documentation via the 'Live Opportunities' list on the e-procurement system, Atamis, available on the following link: https://health-family.force.com/s/Welcome
This exercise is being carried out by NHS South, Central and West Commissioning Support Unit (SCW) on behalf of the Commissioner.
SCW is currently subject to restructuring, and the management of this procurement may therefore move to a successor at some point during the procurement process.  Bidders will be informed of any such change, and any administrative changes because of it.

results.title: EEAST - DPS Framework for Learning and Training Services (24-T23)
results.description:
The East of England Service NHS Trust (“the Authority”) covers the six counties which make up the East of England – Bedfordshire, Cambridgeshire, Essex, Hertfordshire, Norfolk and Suffolk and provides a range of services, but is best known for the 999-emergency service. Our dedicated and skilled staff work 365 days a year, 24 hours a day to make sure patients receive the best possible care.

Our diverse area is spread over about 7,500 square miles and contains a mix of rural, coastal and urban areas – from Watford to Wisbech and Cromer to Canvey Island. Our services are tailored to meet the needs of each community’s differing environmental and medical needs.

The Authority employs more than 5,000 staff and 1,000 volunteers to deal with 1,384,547 emergency calls every year. Staff and volunteers are trained and experienced in caring for patients in a variety of situations, ranging from life-threatening illness and injury to less serious situations such as falls in the home or patients with minor injuries.

In addition, the Authority handles more than one million non-emergency patient journeys to and from routine hospital appointments. Further information regarding the Authority can be obtained from www.eastamb.nhs.uk.

This is a procurement to establish a Dynamic Purchasing System (DPS) of multiple categories and suppliers to provide a range of Learning & Training Services to the Authority.

The contract notice relates to the setting up of a Dynamic Purchasing System (DPS) which will be by the East of England Ambulance Service to procure a range of Learning & Training Services

The Dynamic Purchasing System will be valid until 27th October 2028. Throughout the life of the DPS, the Authority will undertake reviews of its effectiveness and reserves the right to seek new solutions

results.title: CAWT PEACEPLUS EASY Project: Early Intervention Support for Children, Young People and Families presenting with Neurodevelopmental Needs (SHSCT Area)
results.description:
This is a project supported by PEACEPLUS, a programme managed by the Special EU Programmes Body (SEUPB).
The CAWT PEACEPLUS Early Intervention Support Youth Hubs (EASY) project aims to establish new cross border early intervention support services for families with children and young people presenting with traits consistent with a neurodevelopmental type need or who have been recently diagnosed with a neurodevelopmental condition. 
By providing help based on presenting need/symptoms, the project aims to improve outcomes for children, young people and their families by helping families' access appropriate support, based on needs at the right time and in the right place. 
This procurement exercise and the subsequent service to be commissioned will cover only the Northern Ireland delivery area, which is located within the boundaries of the Southern Health and Social Care Trust (SHSCT).
Please refer to the full suite of tender documents for further information on the service requirements.
This tender has been published on the etendersni.gov.uk (https://etendersni.gov.uk) and all tender documentation is available at the following link:
https://etendersni.gov.uk/epps/cft/prepareViewCfTWS.do?resourceId=6534265

results.title: Communal Doors and Door Entry Systems
results.description:
Established in 2004, Procurement for Housing (PfH) is a national procurement consortium dedicated to the social housing sector and supported by the National Housing Federation (NHF), Chartered Institute of Housing (CIH) and HouseMark. Collectively, our Members manage more than 90% of UK' social housing stock, with PfH helping them to achieve efficiency savings using a wide range of services including framework agreements, dynamic purchasing systems, spend analyses, strategy reviews, consolidated billing and comprehensive reporting. PfH is a contracting authority under section 2 of the Procurement Act 2023 and a centralised procurement authority under section 1(4) of that Act.
Please refer to www.pfh.co.uk for additional information.
PfH is administered by Inprova Limited and is headquartered in the North West of England, with over 20 years of expertise and experience offering a complete procurement solutions package across outsourcing, technology and consultancy. By integrating procurement services and technology, Inprova operates as a delivery partner, supporting business performance improvement for the public sector.
PfH is seeking to appoint suitably qualified and experienced organisations under a multi-lot Framework to provide Aluminium/Steel/Stainless Steel/Timber Communal Doors and Audio/Video Door Entry Systems (Wired and Non-Wired). The Framework does not cover non Communal Doors such as front doors for houses or fire doors.
The Framework is structured into 9 Lots and will be awarded for a period of 2 years with two x one year optional extension periods (2+1+1 years).
results.buyer: Procurement for Housing Ltd (t/a PfH Scotland)

results.title: UoD-EFM034-TC-2026 - Water Hygiene Monitoring
results.description:
Estates & Campus Services are required to re-tender the Monitoring, servicing and reactive maintenance contract.  We are seeking another reputable Water hygiene monitoring accredited supplier with a proven record of water hygiene monitoring of domestic and commercial domestic water systems.
The aims and objectives of this contract are to ensure the continuing safety of staff, student's & visitors of the University and the wider public.
This maintenance service is delivered across the University`s Estate comprising the City Centre campus as well as other outlying properties.  All properties are located within the Dundee City boundary.  These properties include an extensive variety of operational data centre and research facilities, teaching facilities, sport facilities and horticultural facilities.
The University believes the Transfer of Undertakings (Protection of Employment) Regulations 2006 (TUPE) may apply to this contract. Tenderers should allow for the transfer of one (1) staff member currently engaged in delivering the water hygiene operational control regime, subject to confirmation through the procurement process. An anonymised TUPE/Employee Liability Information schedule will be provided separately (where applicable). Tenderers must confirm their approach to TUPE, including mobilisation, management arrangements, and integration of the transferring employee into service delivery.
